page: Microsoft Azure E160as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 80 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 1280.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data positions this instance in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 145,445.76. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 14,487.95 GB/sec and large block uncached read and write bandwidths of 462.89 GB/sec and 209.83 GB/sec, respectively. In database and transaction-heavy workloads, the instance achieved 196.39 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a PassMark database operations score of 40,507.49. For language model execution, the server processed 135M model prompts at 5,979.36 tokens per second and 7B model prompts at 370.99 tokens per second.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met using external Premium Storage options, and parallel graphics acceleration is unavailable. This resource profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads by packing a massive 1.28 TB memory footprint alongside 160 dedicated high-frequency AMD EPYC vCPUs, reducing the need for multi-node clustering. The hardware configuration is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, heavy data-decompression pipelines, static web serving at scale, and CPU-based LLM inference.
